items.title: El mar ya no es el mismo de todos los veranos
items.description: A todas las personas que no quieren subirse en ningún tren de actividad estos días. A todas las que han pagado una fortuna por los billetes de avión a un paraíso muy lejano y se dan cuenta, ya en el aeropuerto, de que hay demasiadas maletas, demasiada gente, demasiada comida desperdiciada en las bandejas. A quienes sienten que nos organizamos cada vez mejor para dar una patada al planeta cada vez más fuerte. A quienes les duele el golpe. A los que llegan al destino todavía ilusionados y se encuentran en un rincón del Mediterráneo rodeados de cientos de tiendas idénticas cargadas de los mismos souvenirs de aeropuerto que acaban de dejar atrás. A los que no se rinden y buscan esa foto que justifique todo el esfuerzo y el gasto y las depilaciones y la crema solar protectora que nos recuerda que todo da cáncer , hasta el mismo sol, hasta respirar da cáncer. A quienes suben esa foto que confirma lo que más temían, que las vacaciones ya no sirven para descansar sino para demostrar que has descansado. También a quienes anuncian en Instagram que se cogen unos días, a quienes aseguran que la desconexión es el nuevo lujo e informan de sus escasos días libres de redes como si fueran trabajadores del scroll infinito, tal vez esclavos si es que nadie paga por su trabajo. A todas las poblaciones locales que no pueden alquilar una casa en su tierra porque algún veraneante pagará más por estar menos. A todos los que decidieron salir corriendo de sus ciudades y están parados en medio de no sé qué restaurante o no sé qué parking o no sé qué carretera porque el descanso en 2026 se choca con el muro de la logística. A todos los refugiados climáticos que ya no buscan dónde ir de vacaciones sino dónde queda una esquina para respirar. A mi amigo Rafa, que va a pasarse todo agosto esperando unos pulmones compatibles con una segunda oportunidad para vivir. A todas las personas a quienes la enfermedad les interrumpió la vida este verano. A quienes se enfrentan a un vacío difícil de llenar porque tienen un agujero que solo se puede tapar con un sentido que ya no encuentran. A quienes saben que el sentido a veces coge vacaciones. A todas las parejas que tuvieron la última discusión con este calor y a quienes aún no la han tenido pero la tendrán, a todos los que van a cumplir con la estadística del desamor estival. A aquellos que regresan al mismo mar de todos sus veranos para encontrarse con los niños que fueron en la orilla. Y a quienes se han dado cuenta de que el mar ya no es el mismo de aquellos veranos porque la temperatura ha subido como dos grados y el niño está febril y el mundo enfermo. A todos los que saben que cuando se interrumpe el sentido es obligatorio inventarse uno nuevo, una vida nueva, un verano nuevo. A los valientes que siguen intentándolo. A quienes se animan a tener una buena conversación debajo de un árbol o de una estrella porque saben que nada es tan fascinante ni da tanto miedo ni tanto placer ni nos lleva tan lejos como acercarse a otro ser humano. A los que se atrevieron a hacerlo un verano que aún recuerdan y volverán a hacerlo un verano más. A todos los que leyeron hasta aquí. Vuelvo en septiembre.

items.title: Iran calls for expanding strategic cooperation with Pakistan
items.description: ISLAMABAD: As efforts continue to prevent the conflict in the Gulf from widening, Iran on Friday called for expanding strategic cooperation with Pakistan, describing Islamabad’s diplomatic engagement as an important contribution to regional peace and stability. “Pakistan has played a constructive diplomatic role in facilitating negotiations and advancing efforts towards regional peace and stability,” Iran’s Ambassador to Pakistan Reza Amiri Moghadam said while delivering the keynote address at a roundtable discussion, organised by the Centre for International Strategic Studies. “Strengthening our bilateral cooperation is essential for addressing contemporary security challenges in West Asia,” he said. The discussion, titled Pakistan-Iran Relations and Strategic Stab­i­lity in West Asia, brought together diplomats, academics, defence analysts and researchers to examine the future trajectory of Pakistan-Iran relations against the backdrop of an increasingly volatile regional security environment. Opening the discussion, CISS Exec­utive Director Amb Ali Sarwar Naqvi said the recent escalation had generated fresh uncertainties for regional peace, maritime security and global energy markets, making sustained dialogue and regional engagement more important than ever. Former ambassador Masood Khan said Pakistan’s consistent advocacy of peaceful dispute resolution and its ability to maintain constructive relations with regional and international stakeholders had strengthened its credibility as a facilitator of dialogue, confidence-building measures and de-escalation. Director General of the Institute of Strategic Studies, Islamabad, Amb Moinul Haque said the resilience and national unity displayed by the Iranian people during the recent conflict had played an important role in enabling the country to confront the challenges arising from the crisis. Dr Nazish Mahmood of Quaid-i-Azam University said greater cooperation between Pakistan and Iran in border security, trade, energy and regional connectivity could contribute meaningfully to long-term regional stability. Discussing the maritime dimension of the crisis, retired Rear Admiral Faisal Shah highlighted the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz as one of the world’s principal energy chokepoints and cautioned that prolonged instability there could carry far-reaching consequences for international trade, energy security and maritime stability. Dr Bilal Zubair, director of research at CISS, said the recent conflict had brought Pakistan and Iran closer than ever before, with their shared border, economic interdependence and common concerns over regional instability reinforcing bilateral cooperation and reshaping the relationship across political, economic and strategic domains. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: PM again urges Kabul to act against terrorist groups
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and CDF Field Marshal Asim Munir jointly inaugurate the Sky47 AI Cloud centre.—APP • Says interim Afghan govt has failed to prevent its territory from being used for attacks against Pakistan • Announces Rs300bn Karachi-Chaman dual carriageway, expansion of education, infrastructure and solar projects in Balochistan • Inaugurates Sky47 AI Cloud facility in federal capital ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Sheh­­baz Sharif on Friday again urg­ed Afghanistan to take action agai­nst terrorist organisations and ensu­­re that Afghan soil was not used for terrorist activities against Pakistan. “Pakistan shares over 2,600-kilometre border with its neighbour and has repeatedly urged the Afghan authorities to act against terrorist organisations and prevent Afghan territory from being used against Pakistan. However, the Afghan interim government has failed to take effective action against these groups,” the prime minister said while addressing the National Workshop on Balochistan. The prime minister reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing all possible resources for the development and prosperity of Balochistan, saying Pakistan could only progress when all provinces advanced equally. He announced that the Rs300 billion dual carriageway project from Karachi to Chaman would be completed within two years. Punjab, he said, had contributed Rs150bn to Balochistan under the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award. He added that other provinces had to play their full role in supporting the Balochistan’s development. The premier said Balochistan had been granted an additional 10 per cent quota in the distribution of laptops and scholarships, and that the Kachhi Canal Project would be completed on a fast-track basis. He praised Balochistan’s contributions to Pakistan’s development and prosperity, saying its leadership had always placed the national interest above personal or political considerations and had wholeheartedly supported the federation. He noted that farmers in Baloch­istan had suffered prolonged power outages for years. To address this issue, around 27,000 agricultural tube wells were being converted to solar energy under a Rs75bn project, to which the federal government had contributed Rs50bn. He expressed deep sorrow over the martyrdom of Mastung Judge Abdul Hakeem Kakar and a security official, praying for the elevation of their ranks and for patience for their families. The prime minister alleged that India was financing terrorism inside Pakistan. He added that although terrorism had largely been eliminated by 2017-18, it later resurfaced through what he described as a highly organised conspiracy. AI cloud centre inaugurated Later, PM Shehbaz described the newly inaugurated AI and cloud computing facility as a landmark achievement for Pakistan, reflecting the country’s growing technological capabilities. Addressing the inauguration ceremony of the country’s first-ever Sky47 AI Cloud centre, the prime minister praised the engineers, experts and institutions involved in the project and said the successful execution of the facility showcased the extraordinary talent available in both Pakistan’s military and civilian sectors. Paying tribute to Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir’s leadership, he said the project stood as a testament to what could be achieved when state institutions worked together with a shared national purpose. The prime minister also acknowledged the contributions of Field Marshal Munir, the Ministry of Information Technology, the IT secretary and strategic technology partner ZTE for their roles in delivering the project. The inauguration ceremony was attended by Field Marshal Munir, federal ministers Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Attaullah Tarar, as well as senior government officials. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Petrol price up by Rs3.66, HSD by Rs4.80 as govt revises fuel rates
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday increased the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.66 and Rs4.80 per litre, respectively, passing on the impact of fluctuating global oil prices following renewed hostilities in the Persian Gulf. Following the changes, the price of petrol stands at Rs335.18 per litre, while that of HSD stands at Rs383.46 per litre. The government is charging a total of Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 on diesel. The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 25 (Saturday). The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Prévu sur la base aérienne de Laikipia, dans le centre du pays, ce dispositif a été révélé par la presse américaine en mai. L’affaire a déclenché un tollé au Kenya, avec plusieurs journées de manifestations, alors même que le pays n’a recensé aucun cas du virus. Le verdict est attendu le 26 novembre, alors que la phase des plaidoiries vient tout juste de s’achever.

items.title: Sharifs’ pre-poll promises to AJK don’t sit well with PPP
items.description: • Nawaz, Maryam make development pledges, ‘gift’ of 10 electric buses prompts rigging allegations • In apparent swipe at Bilawal, PML-N supremo says ‘Kashmir should not be mistaken for Kashmore, nor Mirpur for Mirpurkhas’ • PPP assails Nawaz’s remarks, urges Election Commission to take notice of ‘promises’ MUZAFFARABAD: PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif on Friday promised an international airport for Mirpur, the revival of Mansehra-Muzaffarabad-Mirpur mot­o­rway project, and a series of ‘gifts’ for Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), as he and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz made a final campaign push for party’s candidates hours before the electioneering ended for the Mirpur division polls. But the pre-poll promises, and an apparent jibe at PPP chief Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, was not received well by the PML-N’s coalition partner, whose leaders hit back at the elder Sharif, terming his remarks ‘frivolous’ and ‘ridiculous’. Addressing a large public meeting in the lakeside city of Mirpur, the father-daughter duo repeatedly highlighted their Kashmiri roots and told supporters that AJK needed the same infrastructure and welfare-focused governance that had been introduced in Punjab. Describing Kashmir as his “first home”, Mr Sharif said he shared a deep emotional bond with the region. In an apparent swipe at the PPP chairman, Mr Sharif said Kashmir should not be mistaken for Kashmore, nor Mirpur for Mirpurkhas. Mentioning Mr Bhutto-Zardari by name for the first time during his election campaign in AJK, he said: “Don’t take this the wrong way, Bilawal bhai . You are like a son to me.” “Political sparring among parties should continue. There can even be some sharp exchanges, and that’s perfectly healthy. But there should be no fighting or violence.” “We have come with a pledge that, God willing, we will change the destiny of Mirpur and all of Azad Kashmir,” he said, while asking successive governments in Pakistan and AJK what they had done for the region since his ouster. He said the PML-N’s manifesto accorded priority to education and healthcare, promising new schools, colleges and universities as well as hospitals equipped with CT scanners and MRI facilities so that residents would not have to travel to Pakistan for treatment. Nawaz also announced a gift of 10 ‘Hospitals on Wheels’ and as many electric green buses for Mirpur from the Punjab government. He also pledged to dualise the Kotli-Nakyal road, construct tunnels at Lohar Gali and Leepa Valley in Muzaffarabad division, re­­v­­ive the long-stalled motorway project linking Mans­ehra, Muzaffarabad and Mirpur along the Jhelum River, and seek the establishment of an international airport in Mirpur. Speaking after him, CM Maryam argued that AJK did not suffer from a lack of resources but from inadequate infrastructure, insu­fficient welfare program­mes and poor governance. She asked the audience who had built the Kohala-Muzaffarabad Road, the Murree-Kohala Road and cardiac hospitals, prompting chants of “Nawaz Sharif” from the crowd. The Punjab CM pledged that welfare schemes introduced by the PML-N government in Punjab would be extended to AJK immediately after the elections, saying voters should support the party if they wanted development. “The world will see a clean Azad Kashmir after the elections,” she said, urging people to “think carefully” before casting their ballots. PPP hits back The announcement of schemes for AJK, including the ‘gift’ of 10 e-buses, during the campaign did not go well with the PPP. PPP-Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Bukhari strongly criticised the PML-N leadership for gifting 10 electric buses, bearing CM Maryam’s images, to AJK during the election campaign and described the move as “political bribery”. He demanded the chief election commissioner take immediate notice of the transfer of the buses. Some PPP candidates for AJK Assembly elections, including Sardar Javed Ayub, Sardar Mukhtar Abbasi and Syed Bazil Ali Naqvi, also opposed the PML-N move. Taking exception to Mr Sharif’s remarks about the PPP chief, AJK Legislative Assembly Spe­aker and PPP candidate Chaudhry Latif Akbar alleged a series of promises made by PML-N leaders during their election rallies constituted a violation of the election code of conduct, and called on the Election Commission to take strict notice. He told the presser the announcements amounted to an attempt to woo voters ahead of polls. Taking exception to Mr Sharif’s light-hearted remark at a Muzaffarabad rally that he would ask Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to make the PML-N’s nominee the next prime minister of AJK, Mr Akbar quipped: “Nawaz Sharif’s own brother did not make him prime minister, yet he comes here and complains about it.” Referring to Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz’s claims, Mr Akbar alleged the PML-N leadership was attempting to “buy Kashmiri votes” through pre-election promises. Separately, Sindh Information Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon hit back at Mr Sharif’s jibe, saying: “Do not make the land and people of Sindh and Kashmir a subject of ridicule and humour”. Political differences ha­­ve their place, but ridicule of any province, city or area is not acceptable un­­­der any circumstances, he said, terming the ex-PM’s remarks “not only frivolous but also ridiculous”. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Another bid to mend US-Iran fences ‘with China’s blessing’
items.description: TEHRAN: Iranian-made ‘Zulfiqar’ missiles are displayed at Azadi Square. As the US kept up its missile strikes on Iranian targets, the IRGC vowed to ‘kill a member of the US forces for every Iranian killed’.—AFP • Exploratory talks held during Iranian interior minister’s recent Islamabad visit • Dar meets Araghchi at SCO summit; Qatar calls for implementing Islamabad MoU • Beijing concerned as Red Sea closure would compound Hormuz woes • Trump says Iran getting serious about talks; warns China, Russia against ‘getting involved’ in conflict • Says US will punish Iran for attacks on ships by Houthi rebels • Four die as US continues strikes on Iran ISLAMABAD / DUBAI: Pakistan is said to be exploring a path towards a resumption of stalled US-Iran talks to end their nearly five-month-old war, following a push initiated by China. The development came as US missiles struck targets across Iran on Friday after President Donald Trump vowed “major military punishment” for Tehran and its Houthi allies in Yemen for extending the Middle East war to a second major shipping chokepoint, the mouth of the Red Sea. According to Reuters , exploratory discussions for the fresh push towards talks took place during a visit by Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni to Islamabad this week , his second within the last 10 days. Earlier this week, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels had declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia , which signed a mutual defence treaty with Pakistan last year. Beijing, which has consistently backed Pakistan’s mediation efforts, had dispatched its special envoy in March to lead a shuttle-diplomacy trip around the Middle East. China’s interests are being harmed by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and disruptions to the Red Sea route would hit another key trade route Beijing relies on. In a statement, China’s foreign ministry said “China supports the mediation efforts made by Pakistan and other parties.” It added that China will continue to “play an active role in restoring peace and tranquility in the Middle East Gulf region as soon as possible.” Separately, Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani called on all parties to commit to dialogue and to implement the terms of the memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran. This includes “ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, to preserve regional security, safeguard the gains achieved, and enhance regional stability”, the Qatari foreign ministry said. Sheikh Mohammed made the remarks in Doha during a meeting with the new British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband. Implementing the memorandum was necessary to preserve regional security, safeguard the gains achieved and strengthen stability, Sheikh Mohammed said, reiterating Qatar’s full support for efforts to defuse tensions and reach a comprehensive agreement securing lasting peace in the region. ‘Serious about talks’ Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had not decided on whether to launch major strikes on Iran as Tehran was now getting “very serious” in talks with Washington. “Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.” Earlier, in a Truth Social post on Friday, Trump said that he does not believe China or Russia are “participating” in the ongoing Iran conflict, but warned that if they did get inv­o­lved “it would be very bad for them”. Trump also said that he would hold Iran accountable for any further attacks by Yemeni fighters, “and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves”. Iranian media cited the head of Iran’s top joint military command as saying Iran would kill a member of the US forces for every Iranian killed. On Friday, US missiles struck a Revolutionary Guards Navy headquarters in the Ziba Kenar area of the Caspian Sea province of Gilan, according to a security official in Gilan. Provincial authorities said US projectiles had also struck the port city of Bandar Anzali, according to the ILNA news agency. Four people were killed and five injured in a US attack on the Iranian city of Ahvaz, the state broadcaster IRIB said. Diplomatic contacts Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a meeting with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Ara­g­hchi, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s Council of Foreign Ministers Meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan. In a statement, the Foreign Office said the two top diplomats reviewed the ongoing regional situation and bilateral ties. “DPM/FM expressed deep concern over recent regional tensions and underscored the importance of dialogue, restraint, de-escalation by all sides, and sustained diplomatic engagement to achieve lasting peace and stability,” the FO said in a post on X. “He emphasised the need to build on the understandings reached und­er the Islamabad MoU of June 2026.” “The two sides agreed to maintain close coordination and regular consultations on issues of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to working together for regional peace, stability and shared prosperity,” the statement concluded. Separately, in his remarks at the SCO summit, Mr Dar said: “Pakistan firmly believes that dialogue, diplomacy and mutual respect provide the only sustainable way forward to resolve conflicts and achieve durable peace and security.” He added that this principle led to Pakistan hosting talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad in April, “enabling first high-level direct diplomatic contact between the two sides after 47 years”. Mr Dar then urged the international community to seize the opportunity provided by the Islamabad MoU and US-Iran technical talks to push for lasting peace. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Chinese FM meets Tajik counterpart
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Tajik Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin on Friday on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States in Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that in May this year, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon paid a successful state visit to China. The most important outcome of the visit was the signing of the China-Tajikistan Treaty on Permanent Good-Neighborliness, Friendship and Cooperation, which set a precedent in Central Asia, Wang said. The two sides also issued the Joint Statement between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Tajikistan on Deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership in the New Era, demonstrating their determination to jointly promote the building of a China-Tajikistan community with a shared future, Wang said. The common task of the foreign ministries of the two countries is to translate the consensus reached by the two heads of state into concrete actions, make plans for exchanges at various levels, and promote deeper and more substantive cooperation in areas including energy, connectivity and counterterrorism and security, so as to deliver more cooperation outcomes benefiting the people of both countries, Wang said. Muhriddin said Rahmon's visit to China this year was a great success and yielded fruitful results, further consolidating high-level mutual trust, and opening a new chapter in bilateral relations. China has become Tajikistan's largest trade and economic partner, he said, adding that Tajikistan is confident in the prospects of bilateral cooperation. Tajikistan is willing to work with China to fully implement the consensuses reached during Rahmon's visit, strengthen practical cooperation in areas including energy, jointly combat terrorism, and elevate the Tajikistan-China comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership in the new era to a higher level, Muhriddin said.

items.title: SpaceX's Starship rocket lifts off from Texas for 13th test flight
items.description: SpaceX's Starship rocket lifted off from Texas on Friday and deployed its first 20 upgraded Starlink satellites into suborbital ​space, one of many testing goals in the company's 13th test mission as it ‌races to begin routine service with the rocket by the end of the year. The roughly 122-meter-tall Starship rocket system blasted off around 6:50 p.m. ET (2250 GMT) from SpaceX's Starbase company town, with the Super Heavy first stage booster sending its ​Starship upper stage on a suborbital trajectory. The roughly hour-long mission will conclude with Starship's reentry ​through Earth's atmosphere and a splashdown in the Indian Ocean. As Starship approached 26,400 kilometers per hour in space some 10 minutes into its flight, the Super Heavy booster returned ​to Earth and impacted the Gulf of Mexico harder than expected, SpaceX said, though it had reignited more ​engines than its botched return in May during a previous test flight. The Starship test flight is SpaceX's 13th since 2023, featuring a new version of the rocket crucial to the company's plans to expand Starlink, land humans on the moon for ​NASA and eventually deploy thousands of artificial intelligence-processing satellites in orbit. Twenty minutes into its spaceflight, Starship began ​deploying 20 Starlink V3 satellites, dispensing them one by one via the ship's "Pez"-like payload deployment. Flying over a shadowed Earth, ‌thunderstorms ⁠with flashes of lightning were visible in the background 190 kilometers below, according to a camera fixed to the rocket and streamed live by SpaceX. A crowd of SpaceX engineers in SpaceX's Hawthorne, California, facilities could be heard on the live stream cheering at the rocket's mission milestones, at one point chanting "USA." While in ​space, the Starlink satellites – a ​new "V3" version with ⁠greater bandwidth capabilities – will deploy solar arrays and antennae to briefly connect with SpaceX's Starlink network of some 10,000 satellites orbiting above. The Starlinks are the first to ​be deployed by Starship, though they will follow the ship's suborbital trajectory into ​Earth's atmosphere ⁠and burn up. Some of them have spotlights and cameras that will record Starship's heat shield as it hits intense atmospheric friction later in the mission, giving SpaceX key testing insight into how well the rocket survives its ⁠return from ​space. SpaceX plans to use Starship by the end of 2026 ​to begin launching thousands of Starlink V3 satellites, expanding the constellation's capacity to be able to connect directly to mobile devices such ​as cell phones. The current network only connects to Starlink-branded dishes.

items.title: Chinese FM meets Iranian counterpart, urges resumption of negotiations
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with his Iranian counterpart Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Friday, calling for an early resumption of negotiations and the implementation of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East and the Gulf region. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China is deeply concerned about the renewed escalation of tensions in the Middle East and the Gulf region. He said the MoU signed more than a month ago was a valuable outcome of mediation efforts by multiple parties and reflected the aspirations of the Iranian people and other peoples in the region for peace and stability. The progress achieved through dialogue should not be abandoned, he added. "The door to negotiations, once opened, should not be closed, and as long as there is hope for peace, it should not be given up," Wang said. He stressed that the immediate priority is to resolve differences through dialogue and negotiations and resume implementation of the consensus reached in the MoU. As a comprehensive strategic partner of Iran, China firmly supports Iran in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and national dignity, Wang said. He added that China will continue to act in line with the four-point proposal on maintaining and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, support mediation efforts by Pakistan and other parties, facilitate the early resumption of dialogue and negotiations, properly address issues related to the Strait of Hormuz, improve relations among neighboring countries, advance collective security among Gulf states and help restore peace and stability in the Middle East at an early date. Araghchi briefed Wang on the latest developments in the Middle East and the Gulf region, stressing that Iran's willingness to negotiate remains unchanged and Tehran does not wish to see the conflict continue. He urged the United States to honor its commitments, exercise restraint, work with Iran toward the same goal and seek a reasonable solution. Araghchi said it is crucial for Iran and China, as comprehensive strategic partners, to strengthen communication and coordination at the current critical moment. He thanked China for consistently maintaining an objective and impartial position and promoting peace and dialogue, and expressed hope that China would continue to play an important role in helping ease regional tensions.

items.title: Chinese FM Wang Yi meets Pakistani counterpart
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Friday on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States in Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China-Pakistan relations have always remained at the forefront of the times. The two sides should jointly implement the important consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries, actively advance exchanges at all levels and cooperation across various fields, and accelerate the building of an even closer China-Pakistan community with a shared future, Wang said. China highly appreciates Pakistan's key role in facilitating the memorandum of understanding reached between the United States and Iran, Wang said, adding that China will continue to firmly support Pakistan in its efforts to mediate, promote the return of all parties to dialogue and negotiations, and achieve a lasting ceasefire. China is ready to strengthen coordination with Pakistan on multilateral platforms such as the SCO and the United Nations to safeguard the common interests of the two countries and the legitimate rights and interests of the Global South, Wang said. Dar said it is essential for Pakistan and China to maintain communication and coordination on all occasions. The sudden escalation of the situation in the Middle East and the Gulf serves the interests of no party, he said, adding that Pakistan is willing to continue its efforts in peace mediation and appreciates China's consistent support and assistance. Pakistan is ready to strengthen coordination with China under multilateral frameworks such as the SCO and the China-Pakistan-Bangladesh trilateral cooperation mechanism, and make due contributions to safeguarding regional peace, stability and development, he said.

items.title: Chinese FM Wang Yi meets Russian counterpart
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on Friday on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States in Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that the meeting between the two heads of state in May in Beijing has ushered bilateral relations into a new stage of greater achievements and faster development. China wishes Russia success in its State Duma elections to be held in September and firmly supports the choice independently made by the Russian people, Wang said. Noting that this year marks the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation and the 25th anniversary of the SCO, Wang said the treaty has guided the two countries in setting an example of a new type of state-to-state and major-country relations. The SCO has become a force for global stability with growing international influence, Wang said, adding that both sides should jointly support the organization's development, carry forward the Shanghai Spirit and inject new vitality into improving global governance and building a community with a shared future for humanity. China and Russia should strengthen strategic coordination, uphold the outcomes of World War II and never allow Japan to rearm, Wang said, adding that he expected Russia to continue supporting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) "China Year" events, and called for closer coordination and mutual support in multilateral frameworks including the United Nations. Lavrov said head-of-state diplomacy serves as an important driving force for Russia-China relations. President Putin's successful visit to China this year and the more than 50 meetings between the two heads of state have continuously elevated bilateral relations to new heights, he said. He congratulated China on successfully hosting the World Artificial Intelligence (AI) Conference, noting that Russia has joined the World AI Cooperation Organization and looks forward to deepening bilateral cooperation in innovation and science and technology through this platform. Russia remains highly vigilant against and firmly opposes Japan's accelerated remilitarization and pursuit of nuclear weapons capability, he said. The two sides can further strengthen strategic coordination within multilateral frameworks such as the United Nations, APEC, the Group of Twenty, BRICS and East Asia Cooperation, and jointly promote a more democratic and equitable multipolar world, he added. The two sides also had an in-depth exchange of views on international and regional issues of common concern.

items.title: Les caniveaux ne votent pas, mais ils parlent
items.description: © Internet À chaque hivernage, Bamako reçoit le même avertissement. Les rues se remplissent d’eau, des habitations sont envahies et les dégâts relancent le débat sur l’assainissement. La pluie déclenche la crise, mais elle n’en explique pas à elle seule l’ampleur. Les réseaux de drainage insuffisants, les collecteurs mal entretenus et les constructions érigées dans certains passages naturels de l’eau relèvent de la responsabilité publique. Mais il existe aussi une responsabilité plus proche, plus quotidienne et souvent plus difficile à reconnaître. Celle du citoyen qui transforme le caniveau en poubelle. Un sachet jeté dans la rue paraît insignifiant. Ajouté à des milliers d’autres, il finit pourtant par ralentir l’écoulement, obstruer un passage et aggraver les conséquences d’une forte pluie. Salir aujourd’hui et réclamer demain une ville propre constitue une contradiction que l’on ne peut plus ignorer. Aucun État, aussi efficace soit-il, ne peut construire une ville contre ses propres habitants. Les autorités doivent construire des ouvrages adaptés, assurer la collecte des ordures, curer régulièrement les caniveaux et sanctionner les dépôts anarchiques. Mais aucune politique d’assainissement ne peut produire des résultats durables si les ouvrages nettoyés sont aussitôt remplis de déchets. La responsabilité commence aussi devant les maisons, dans les marchés, le long des rues et autour des dépôts improvisés. La pluie est un phénomène naturel. Les infrastructures défaillantes relèvent de l’action publique. Jeter ses ordures dans un caniveau est un choix individuel. Les inondations naissent souvent de la rencontre de ces trois réalités. Les prévenir suppose donc moins de désignation et davantage de responsabilités partagées. Salimata Wagué

items.description: ERIC LEE / THE NEW YORK TIMES

items.title: Trump’s Trigger Warnings
items.description: Incensed by the Smithsonian but lacking immediate power to do anything about it, Donald Trump has resorted to trolling the world’s largest museum complex from the sidewalk. In an executive order posted this afternoon, the president directed the Department of the Interior to place signs outside the National Museum of American History warning passersby about “ideological capture” and detailing the findings of his administration’s recent, quickly contested report on the museum. The order comes days after the museum’s director, Anthea Hartig, was grilled by lawmakers on Capitol Hill. The warnings, the order says, will direct visitors to “locations and resources for accurate information” about American history and will notify them that exhibits “should be renovated consistent with the findings of the Report.” It asserts that the “current leadership of both the Smithsonian Institution and the Museum cannot be trusted to tell America’s story with honesty and gratitude.” Having determined, perhaps, that the museum’s 250-object exhibit “exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence” is not enough, Trump also ordered the Department of the Interior to mount its own temporary exhibits outside that will “appropriately honor the 56 signers” of the document. To the White House, the order is probably meant to escalate its public-pressure campaign on the Smithsonian, which began with an executive order last spring calling to rid the institution of “improper ideology” and restore it “to its rightful place as a symbol of inspiration and American greatness.” In short, Trump feels that the museums are too negative about the country’s history and should be more patriotic, and the Smithsonian argues that its museums can be celebratory and present complex stories at the same time. Instead, the call to place trigger warnings outside the museum reflects the limitations of the Trump administration’s power in this instance, as well as a weakness in its campaign to seize control of the American story. The Smithsonian occupies a strange place as a public-private partnership and “independent federal trust instrumentality” of the U.S. government. Partially funded by the federal government, the institution is governed by a board of regents, which does not have presidential appointees and can’t be purged in the way that the board of the Kennedy Center was . Although in some specific cases the Smithsonian has been treated as part of the executive branch and in others it has not, the institution is not an executive agency and not overseen by the president like the National Park Service is (NPS is managed by the Interior Department). That means the Smithsonian is also not susceptible to the type of mandated history scrubbing that NPS leadership has enforced at historic sites across the country. Trump is directing Interior Secretary Doug Burgum in this new order because he cannot officially direct Hartig, and neither can he direct Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch, who reports to the board of regents. The signs will go on the NPS-controlled sidewalks and walkways because that’s where the White House can have a say. The White House looks to even be aware of these limitations in the executive order, urging the heads of the Interior Department, the Office of Management and Budget, and the General Services Administration, as well as the assistant to the president for domestic policy to “identify and utilize any and all available authorities to promote the policy of this order.” This includes “any mechanisms available to encourage correction of the issues identified in the Report.” The naming of the OMB appears to nod to previous threats that the White House has made about hinging the Smithsonian’s apportioned funds on its compliance with Trump’s vision, which likely would be illegal. In its July 4 report on the American-history museum, the White House argued, essentially, that the museum has been politicized and that it “no longer treats the American story as a shared national inheritance to be taught or celebrated, but as a political instrument to divide, dispirit, and discourage our citizens.” It criticizes what it calls “anti-White” advocacy and takes specific aim at museum representations of transgender Americans and undocumented immigrants, as well as exhibits featuring Filipino and Mexican Americans, describing as activism what many might simply see as mentions of people who exist in this country. The report repeatedly calls out museum staffers by name, and Hartig appears in more than a dozen images throughout the document. Speaking in one of the congressional hearings this week, Representative Melanie Stansbury, a New Mexico Democrat, called it “a political witch hunt.” During those dizzying hearings, Hartig tried to defend her and her colleagues’ work. She told lawmakers that the museum is nonpartisan, and that it uses “historical evidence” and “competing perspectives” and acknowledges “enduring debates.” She said that the museum’s goal is to “preserve and document the evidence of American life in all of its breadth, so that the public can encounter the past and draw their own conclusions,” and that telling the full story of history “is a form of respect for the American people.” None of this, of course, stopped the accusations of activism or a GOP witness and even one lawmaker from calling for a cleaning-out of the institution’s leadership. The hearing was theater. The signs are too. A kind of turf war has taken place across the National Mall this summer. The Great American State Fair , the signs plastered with Trump’s slogan “We are making D.C. Safe and Beautiful,” and the ever troubled Reflecting Pool —the president’s hand has been ubiquitous in America’s backyard. Still, these incoming signs will mark a new kind of outward hostility, falling somewhere closer to putting Trump’s name on the Kennedy Center. To publicly take aim at a beloved American institution could risk doing exactly what Trump accuses the Smithsonian of in the report: dividing. But there’s something that the president, it seems, has not considered. Trump and his coterie love to talk about “freedom-loving” Americans, and those freedom-loving Americans don’t exactly love being told what to do. Some of them might even see these signs outside the museum and have all the more reason to walk right on in.

items.title: Protection sociale : les journalistes face au défi de l’affiliation
items.description: © JDM Réunis le 24 juillet 2026 au Mémorial Modibo Keïta de Bamako, professionnels des médias, pouvoirs publics et organismes sociaux ont examiné les obstacles à la couverture sociale des journalistes. La rencontre intervient dans un secteur où la précarité contractuelle prive encore une grande partie des travailleurs de l’assurance maladie, des prestations familiales et de la retraite. L’Union des journalistes reporters du Mali (UJRM) a organisé, vendredi 24 juillet 2026, une journée de réflexion sur la protection sociale des professionnels des médias. Tenue en prélude à la cinquième édition de la Nuit de l’UJRM, la rencontre avait pour thème « Journalisme et précarité : entre devoir et déboires ». Elle a bénéficié de l’appui de la Fondation Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung. Les échanges se sont appuyés sur une réalité déjà documentée par l’organisation. Une enquête menée par l’UJRM en 2025 auprès de 200 journalistes à Bamako et dans huit autres localités indiquait que 63 % des répondants ne disposaient pas d’un contrat de travail formel. Elle établissait également que 74,5 % ne bénéficiaient d’aucune couverture sociale et que la moitié travaillait sans rémunération stable. La journée a porté sur les dispositions du Code du travail, le Code de prévoyance sociale, les démarches d’affiliation et les difficultés rencontrées par les entreprises de presse pour déclarer régulièrement leurs employés. Le cadre légal impose pourtant à l’employeur de s’affilier au régime de prévoyance sociale et de faire immatriculer ses salariés. La rencontre a réuni notamment Bandiougou Danté, président de la Maison de la presse, Mohamed Ag Albachar, chef de cabinet du ministre de la Communication, de l’Économie numérique et de la Modernisation de l’Administration, ainsi que des représentants de l’Institut national de prévoyance sociale. Les travaux ont été modérés par le journaliste Salif Sanogo. Dans sa présentation, Sékou Issa Diarra, inspecteur de sécurité sociale à l’INPS, a détaillé les prestations auxquelles l’affiliation peut ouvrir droit. Elles concernent notamment les risques professionnels, les prestations familiales et la retraite. Il a insisté sur la régularité des déclarations et des cotisations, indispensable au maintien effectif des droits des travailleurs. Pour le président de l’UJRM, Boubacar Kanouté, la question ne se limite pas aux revenus. Elle touche aussi à la stabilité professionnelle et à la capacité du journaliste à faire face à la maladie, à un accident ou à la fin de sa carrière. « Un journaliste qui exerce sans couverture en cas de maladie, d’accident professionnel ou sans garantie pour son avenir reste exposé à une grande vulnérabilité », a-t-il déclaré. Mohamed Ag Albachar a présenté la protection sociale comme une condition nécessaire à l’exercice d’une presse professionnelle et responsable. Il a reconnu que les difficultés économiques des médias freinent encore la formalisation de nombreux emplois et appelé à une action associant les pouvoirs publics, les employeurs, les organisations professionnelles et les partenaires. Le représentant de la Fondation Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung a également insisté sur la responsabilité partagée des différents acteurs. Les discussions ont principalement porté sur la formalisation des contrats de travail, l’affiliation effective des journalistes et le versement régulier des cotisations sociales. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: Secrétariat général de l’ONU : Macky Sall dévoile sa feuille de route !
items.description: Quelques jours après avoir obtenu le soutien officiel du Sénégal à sa candidature au poste de Secrétaire général des Nations unies, l'ancien président Macky Sall accélère sa campagne diplomatique. Dans une déclaration rendue publique jeudi, il a présenté les grandes priorités qui guideraient ses premiers jours de mandat s'il était élu à la tête de l'organisation. L'ancien chef de l'État sénégalais affirme vouloir agir rapidement afin de « restaurer la confiance » au sein des Nations unies. Une priorité qu'il considère indispensable dans un contexte marqué par la multiplication des conflits, les tensions géopolitiques, les crises climatiques et les difficultés de financement auxquelles fait face l'institution. Selon lui, les premiers jours d'un mandat doivent envoyer un signal fort. Son programme prévoit notamment une consultation des différentes composantes du système onusien, une évaluation des réformes en cours ainsi que l'ouverture de discussions avec les États membres afin d'améliorer l'efficacité et la crédibilité de l'organisation. Cette prise de parole intervient dans un contexte politique particulier. Lundi dernier, le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a officiellement annoncé que le Sénégal soutenait la candidature de son prédécesseur, qualifiant cette ambition de candidature portée au service du Sénégal, de l'Afrique et du multilatéralisme. Macky Sall avait salué cette décision, y voyant un geste d'unité nationale au-delà des divergences politiques. En choisissant de détailler son agenda dès les premiers jours d'un éventuel mandat, Macky Sall cherche également à se distinguer des autres candidats en présentant une vision concrète plutôt qu'un simple programme de principes. Cette démarche s'inscrit dans une campagne où la capacité à proposer des réformes crédibles sera déterminante auprès des États membres appelés à désigner le successeur d'António Guterres. Toutefois, cette candidature continue de susciter des réactions contrastées au Sénégal. Si elle bénéficie désormais du soutien officiel de l'État, plusieurs organisations de victimes des violences politiques des années 2021-2024 continuent d'exprimer leur opposition, estimant que les procédures judiciaires doivent suivre leur cours avant toute consécration internationale. En présentant une feuille de route centrée sur la restauration de la confiance, l'efficacité administrative et la réforme du multilatéralisme, Macky Sall poursuit désormais une campagne résolument tournée vers la scène internationale, où chaque prise de parole vise à convaincre les États membres de sa capacité à conduire les Nations unies dans un environnement mondial particulièrement instable.

items.title: West Bank: Surge in Settler Violence Threatens Mass Atrocities
items.description: (Beirut) – Two Israeli settler attacks on Tal village near Nablus in the West Bank on July 24, 2026, resulted in the killing of four Palestinians and two Israelis, Human Rights Watch said today. The incident triggered a wave of settler reprisal attacks in nearby Palestinian villages, the Israeli government’s announcement of a “major counterterrorism operation,” and Israeli officials calling for the destruction of Palestinian homes and villages. Concerned governments should urgently act to prevent further settler violence and atrocities. “The Israeli government didn’t prevent the settler attacks on Tal village, so now it needs to stop settler reprisals and escalating military action that will make a bad situation worse,” said Sarah Sanbar, acting Israel and Palestine researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Years of lawlessness and impunity for attacks has turned the West Bank into a powder keg waiting to explode, and decisive action is urgently needed.” The July 24 killings in Tal bring the Palestinian death toll in the occupied West Bank since July 19 to 10. As of July 19, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026, at least 13 by settlers. OCHA reported that as of July 15, 20 Israelis had been injured in 2026 in the West Bank. Settler violence has risen sharply since the current Israeli government took office in October 2022, with the most recent spike in March and April 2026, during the United States and Israel’s war with Iran. Human Rights Watch interviewed two witnesses to the attacks and a local activist, and verified six videos of the incidents posted to social media platforms and shared directly with researchers. Between 6:10 and 6:45 a.m. on July 24, 40 to 50 settlers, including children, approached Tal from the east, attacked four or five Palestinian homes with stones, and tried to break in, witnesses said. A confrontation between the settlers and Palestinians erupted, during which an armed settler shot and wounded a Palestinian man, the witnesses said. More Palestinians then arrived to assist the family, and the settlers fled. About 30 minutes later, the same group of settlers reentered Tal from the southwest, where they were joined by Israeli soldiers, said Mujahid Waleed, a local resident who witnessed both incidents. “When I arrived [to the second location], the settlers and the Palestinians were already fighting,” Waleed said. “The settlers were attacking the Palestinians, and the army stood by and didn’t intervene. The army only intervened once a Palestinian man disarmed a settler and started shooting at the soldier and settlers. The army fired back and killed point-blank the [Palestinian] carrying the weapon, and settlers and soldiers shot the other three unarmed Palestinians.” The attacks took place in Area B, an area under joint Israeli-Palestinian Authority security control under the Oslo II Accords. The four Palestinians killed were two brothers and two cousins from the Ramadan family. Human Rights Watch verified and geolocated two videos showing the confrontation that are consistent with Waleed’s account. One video shows two armed settlers alongside a uniformed soldier, close to a group of Palestinian men. The settlers apparently start the physical altercation, kicking a Palestinian man before a fight breaks out and a soldier fires into the air. When two Palestinian men try to take the settlers’ weapons, gunshots are heard and a Palestinian man falls to the ground. A settler is seen holding a raised weapon. A second video shows the second Palestinian man taking a firearm from a settler and pushing him to the ground; the settler draws a handgun, and the Palestinian man appears to fire at him. The Israeli military stated at 9:32 a.m. that soldiers were dispatched to the area following a report regarding “an attack on Israeli civilians who were hiking in the area” and that “terrorists stole the weapon of a security personnel who had arrived at the scene and opened fire toward the Israeli civilians.” The military later announced that the incident resulted in the killing of Benyahu Mellet, 32, and Maj. Yuval Ezra, 27, an active-duty soldier. The Israeli military said the platoon commander returned fire and killed the Palestinian gunman, the Times of Israel reported. It did not provide details about the killing of the other three Palestinians. Human Rights Watch, other nongovernmental organizations, and the media have repeatedly reported attacks by armed settlers that often occur alongside Israeli army units or with soldiers standing by and failing to intervene. They found that settlers responsible for attacks often operate with the financial, material, and legal backing of the Israeli state. The Times of Israel reported that Mellet headed the civil defense squad of the Havat Gilad settlement. Following October 7, 2023, the National Security Ministry established these squads in West Bank settlements and gave them special policing powers, uniforms, and weapons. The squads’ establishment, along with settler-only “regional defense battalions” in the Israeli military, have contributed to the dangerous blurring of the line between settlers and soldiers. In response to the incident, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu convened an emergency security meeting, announced the redeployment of five military battalions to the West Bank, and directed the military to carry out an “intensive counterterrorism operation.” Since then, settler reprisal attacks have been reported in nearbyvillages, the Palestinian news agency WAFA reported. The attacks have resulted in injuries, arson, and other property damage. Netanyahu also announced that he would accelerate the regularization of settler outposts and the establishment of new ones. These outposts, which have often served as launching pads for attacks on Palestinian communities, are illegal under both Israeli law and the Fourth Geneva Convention. Their retroactive legalization serves to push the frontier of settlement expansion and enable the appropriation of Palestinian land, often serving as precursors to larger settlements. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called on Netanyahu to “allow the establishment of a settlement at the Sela outpost, near the place where the severe attack took place this morning. To this end, it is necessary to transfer this area from Area B to Area C [fully Israeli-controlled territory], take responsibility for it and allow a settlement to be established there.” Since the attack, Israeli officials have issued statements calling for the destruction of Palestinian homes and villages. Smotrich said the villages “should look like the refugee camps in Nablus and Tulkarem,” which were destroyed during an Israeli military operation in January 2025 that Human Rights Watch found amounted to war crimes, crimes against humanity, and ethnic cleansing. In a post on X, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said: “The cities and villages of the killers in the West Bank should be treated the same way Beit Hanoun [an embattled Palestinian town] was treated in Gaza. ... For every Jew murdered - the enemy must absorb the loss of lands and homes.” In July 2024, the International Court of Justice found that Israel’s occupation of Palestinian territory is unlawful and that Israel is in breach of the prohibition of racial segregation and apartheid. The court found Israel has an obligation to evacuate all settlers in the West Bank including East Jerusalem, allow displaced Palestinians to return to their homes, and provide them with reparations. Governments should urgently act to prevent further atrocities across the West Bank, including by imposing targeted sanctions on those implicated in ongoing grave abuses, suspending arms transfers to Israel, banning trade with illegal settlements, suspending preferential trade agreements with Israel, and supporting the International Criminal Court and its ongoing investigations, including by executing its arrest warrants. “The settler violence against Tal is a reminder that if the violence is not stopped and those responsible are not held to account, escalation and further atrocities are inevitable,” Sanbar said. “Governments need to act urgently so that the Israeli government does not continue to act as if it has a green light to commit further atrocities.”

items.title: The Saudis Learn the Truth About Trump
items.description: Faithless, chaotic, and corrupt: Donald Trump's character also shapes his foreign policy. The latest victim is Saudi Arabia—not a sympathetic victim, maybe, but a victim all the same. On July 22, United States Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart signed an agreement for a Saudi-U.S. civilian nuclear partnership. The multi-decade, multibillion-dollar deal allows American companies to develop and operate commercial nuclear power plants on Saudi soil, potentially including a uranium-enrichment facility. The Saudis have sought such a deal for almost 20 years. United States presidents from Barack Obama onward have expressed openness to it, but on two conditions: Any deal must include safeguards against Saudi use of enrichment for nuclear weapons and also a normalization of relations with Israel. With the return of Donald Trump to the presidency in 2024, the Saudis surely hoped their moment had arrived. Saudi Arabia has invested heavily in Trump and the Trump family, including licensing deals with the Trump Organization potentially worth billions of dollars and a huge commitment to the private-equity firm founded by Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner. This week, those investments seemed to have paid off. Details on Wednesday’s agreement are sparse, but The Washington Post reported that the pact, by clearing a way to nuclear enrichment, opened a path to an eventual Saudi nuclear weapon. The deal also reportedly dropped the precondition that Saudi Arabia recognize Israel. [ Read: The art of the giveaway ] The Saudis, essentially, had got everything they wanted, with little sacrifice in return. But no sooner was the deal signed than the reneging began. In a Truth Social post yesterday, Trump insisted that the deal did not, in fact, include uranium enrichment and that it is “totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords”—that is, to normalized relations with Israel. Utter chaos and confusion duly erupted over what Trump meant to accomplish with these words. Is Trump attempting to blow up the freshly inked deal after hearing Republicans criticize it on Fox News and elsewhere, as CNN suggests ? Or was the outburst simply Trump bluster without real-world consequences? No one seems to know. Trump did not consult the Saudi leadership before adding a late condition to the deal they had just celebrated. Just what this means for the deal’s fate in Congress is unclear too. Congress can block it, but would need a veto-proof majority in both the House and Senate to do so—presuming Trump even wants the deal to go ahead. The Saudis must be puzzled. They paid their “quid” to the Trump family. Where is their “quo”? Can criticism on Fox News cancel billions paid for the Trump family’s favor? This turnabout comes at a very bad time for Saudi Arabia. The country has already been left stranded and exposed by the failure of Trump’s Iran war, which has emboldened Iran and tightened its hold on the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia’s most important maritime connection to world oil markets. Saudi Arabia needs protection. Its traditional protector has been exposed as fickle and weak. The kingdom may now see a nuclear force of its own as a condition of its survival in a post-American Middle East. [ Read: The mess the Iran War made ] American advocates of a U.S.-Saudi nuclear deal have long warned that if the United States does not partner with Saudi Arabia, the Saudis might look to Russia or China for nuclear technology and stronger military ties. But past Saudi efforts to find alternative security arrangements have not worked well. In 2023, Saudi Arabia signed a Chinese-brokered rapprochement with Iran, but China’s friendly relations with Tehran did nothing to protect Saudi Arabia from Iranian missile attacks in recent months. Saudi Arabia’s other options look even worse. The country, which reportedly financed the Pakistani nuclear-weapons program in the 1990s, is believed to hold some kind of call on those weapons if it ever needs them. The two countries formalized a joint defense pact last year. But a future as a Pakistani military protectorate is not a promising one, especially because India ranks among Saudi Arabia’s top three export markets, and is probably its fastest-growing one. Which brings us back to Saudi Arabia’s Plan A. Is the nukes plan cooked? Trump often announces things on social media that don’t come true in real life. In his first term, he announced on Twitter in 2019 that he had ordered all U.S. businesses out of China. The “order” was dropped three days later. In June 2025, Trump announced a pause on immigration enforcement on farms, and at hotels and restaurants. The pause was reversed several days later. Trump has repeatedly announced tariff increases that are then shelved and military strikes that are never carried out, including a vow last November to invade Nigeria “guns a-blazing” to wipe out that country’s Islamic insurgents. So it may be with Trump’s after-the-signature demand that Saudi Arabia recognize Israel as an additional price for a deal greased by the flow of funds to Trump companies and relatives. America’s traditional democratic allies feel betrayed and baffled by the unpredictability of Trump’s pay-for-play diplomacy. But those willing to pay can suffer betrayals and bafflements of their own. If not even the Saudis, who showered Trump and his family with cash and gifts, can trust Trump’s diplomacy, who else on earth can feel any confidence at all?

items.title: Ioba/Dissihn : le vice-gouverneur de la BCEAO offre trois millions de francs CFA à l’initiative Faso Mêbo
items.description: Ioba/Dissihn : le vice-gouverneur de la BCEAO offre trois millions de francs CFA à l'initiative Faso Mêbo Dissihn, 24 juil. 2026 (AIB)-Le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Dissihn, Benjamin Nana, a réceptionné, le 4 juillet 2026, un don de trois millions de francs CFA offert par le vice-gouverneur de la Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO), Kpièlè Der Rogatien Poda. Le donateur répond ainsi à l'appel du président du Faso, Ibrahim Traoré, qui invite les Burkinabè à construire et développer la nation par eux-mêmes. Le vice-gouverneur de la BCEAO, Kpièlè Der Rogatien Poda, en séjour dans sa famille, a vu son passage coïncider avec le lancement officiel des travaux de Faso Mêbo dans la commune de Dissihn. « Je suis natif de cette localité et c'est par hasard que je découvre cette activité bien heureuse que vous menez. Faso Mêbo est une initiative louable, c'est pourquoi j'ai décidé d'apporter ma contribution financière et de participer aux travaux », a-t-il confié. Pour son attachement à son village et à son pays, il a offert un chèque d'une valeur de trois millions (3 000 000) de FCFA pour soutenir l'initiative Faso Mêbo. En plus du chèque, il a donné la somme de vingt mille (20 000) FCFA pour le rafraîchissement des citoyens mobilisés pour la confection des pavés. Le PDS de la commune de Dissihn, Benjamin Nana, a salué le geste du donateur, qu'il a qualifié de patriotique. « Vous venez de poser un acte citoyen. Je vous remercie pour votre engagement patriotique. J'invite les fils et filles de Dissihn où qu'ils se trouvent à accompagner les efforts de développement de notre commune », a-t-il déclaré. Les autorités communales ont rappelé que les dons en faveur de l'initiative Faso Mêbo continuent d'être reçus à la mairie de Dissihn. Agence d'Information du Burkina JBD/SZ-ATA

items.title: Recours sur la finale de la CAN 2025 : pourquoi le TAS a fixé une audience à huis clos
items.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a annoncé, vendredi 24 juillet, la tenue de l'audience dans la procédure opposant la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF) à la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) et à la Fédération royale marocaine de football (FRMF) au sujet de la finale de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations (CAN) 2025. Selon le communiqué du TAS, l'audience se déroulera le 8 octobre 2026 à son siège de Lausanne, en Suisse. Cette procédure fait suite à l'appel déposé par la FSF le 25 mars 2026 contre la décision de la CAF ayant déclaré le Sénégal perdant de la finale par forfait (3-0) au profit du Maroc. La Fédération sénégalaise demande l'annulation de cette décision et sollicite du TAS qu'il la reconnaisse vainqueur de la CAN 2025. Le TAS précise que les parties ne sont pas parvenues à un accord sur une procédure accélérée. Le dossier suivra donc le calendrier habituel prévu par les règles de l'institution. Après consultation des parties, il a également été décidé que l'audience se tiendra à huis clos, aucune demande de publicité des débats n'ayant été formulée. À l'issue de l'audience, la formation arbitrale entamera ses délibérations. Le TAS indique toutefois qu'il n'est pas en mesure de préciser la date à laquelle sa sentence sera rendue, tout en soulignant qu'aucune décision ne sera prononcée le jour même de l'audience. Enfin, le Tribunal arbitral du sport appelle à la prudence face aux informations circulant sur cette affaire. Il rappelle que seules les communications publiées sur ses canaux officiels font foi et que toute annonce relative à cette procédure sera diffusée par ses services. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Sandbondtenga/Gestion des ressources partagées : la commune de Ziga valide le projet de Charte foncière locale du Royaume de Boussouma
items.description: Sandbondtenga/Gestion des ressources partagées : la commune de Ziga valide le projet de Charte foncière locale du Royaume de Boussouma Ziga, 21 juillet 2026 (AIB)-La Délégation spéciale communale de Ziga a validé, mardi, le projet de Charte foncière locale (CFL) du Royaume de Boussouma, lors de sa première session extraordinaire, marquant une étape importante du processus de consultation des collectivités territoriales concernées par ce futur référentiel de gestion foncière. Au terme d'échanges approfondis sur le document de 115 articles présenté par le secrétaire général de la mairie de Ziga, le camarade Clément Savadogo, les membres de la Délégation spéciale ont validé à l'unanimité le projet soumis à leur appréciation. Cette validation s'inscrit dans le processus d'élaboration de cet instrument destiné à encadrer la gestion et la préservation des ressources naturelles d'utilisation commune, notamment les forêts villageoises, les pistes à bétail, les zones de pâture, les retenues d'eau, les bois sacrés et les sites aurifères. Selon le camarade Savadogo, cette charte, fondée sur les us et coutumes du Royaume de Boussouma, constitue « un levier de prévention et de gestion des conflits fonciers pour la promotion d'un vivre-ensemble harmonieux entre les communautés ». Élaborée avec l'accompagnement de l'Observatoire national du foncier du Burkina Faso (ONF-BF), la Charte foncière locale traduit les règles coutumières régissant la gestion des terres dans le Royaume de Boussouma, tout en restant conforme aux textes législatifs et réglementaires en vigueur. Pour le président de la Délégation spéciale communale de Ziga, le camarade Amadou Konvolobo, cette validation représente la contribution de la commune au processus de consultation engagé dans l'ensemble des collectivités territoriales relevant du Royaume de Boussouma, avant l'adoption officielle de la charte par les instances coutumières. La Charte foncière locale se veut un référentiel participatif de prévention et de gestion des conflits fonciers, élaboré de manière concertée avec les autorités coutumières, les collectivités territoriales et les services techniques déconcentrés. Elle ambitionne de sécuriser les droits d'accès et d'usage de la terre, de renforcer le dialogue entre les acteurs coutumiers et institutionnels et de consolider durablement la cohésion sociale au sein des communautés. Agence d'Information du Burkina SFS/aio/ata

items.title: Koulsé/Reconnaissance nationale : les forces vives outillées sur les droits des héros, martyrs et invalides de la Nation
items.description: Koulsé/Reconnaissance nationale : les forces vives outillées sur les droits des héros, martyrs et invalides de la Nation Kaya, 23 juillet 2026 (AIB)-La secrétaire générale de la région des Koulsé, Bernadette Adenyo/Sermé, a présidé jeudi à Kaya un atelier régional de vulgarisation des lois portant statuts de héros, de martyr, d'invalide et de pupille de la Nation, pour renforcer la connaissance et l'appropriation de ces textes par les forces vives de la région. Organisée par le Secrétariat de la commission nationale d'analyse et de suivi des dossiers de héros, de martyr et d'invalide de la Nation, cette session de deux jours réunit 75 participants issus des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), des services déconcentrés de l'État, des organisations de la société civile, des autorités coutumières et religieuses, ainsi que des associations de femmes, de jeunes, de veuves et d'orphelins. À l'ouverture des travaux, Mme Adenyo/Sermé a salué le choix de la région des Koulsé, qu'elle considère comme un symbole de résilience face à la crise sécuritaire. Elle a estimé que ces textes traduisent la reconnaissance de la Nation envers ceux qui ont consenti le sacrifice suprême pour la défense de la patrie et la protection de leurs ayants droit, invitant les participants à s'approprier les dispositions légales afin de mieux orienter les bénéficiaires. La camarade Pingdbamba Esther Somé/Kiema, chef du département de la gouvernance administrative, juridique, institutionnelle et politique à la Primature, a indiqué que l'atelier sera marqué par des communications consacrées aux droits et privilèges attachés aux statuts de héros, de martyr, d'invalide et de pupille de la Nation, ainsi qu'aux procédures de leur reconnaissance. Pour elle, ces lois visent à « valoriser les efforts consentis par les citoyens dans la défense de la patrie », à « honorer la mémoire de ceux qui sont tombés pour la défense de la patrie » et à assurer la protection de leurs familles. Elle a appelé les participants à devenir des relais de vulgarisation afin que les ayants droit connaissent les mécanismes de reconnaissance et les démarches de saisine de la Commission nationale. Agence d'Information du Burkina AIO/ata
